styles.a: 1980s science-fiction paperback and game-box cover art: airbrushed acrylic painting, smooth gradients, warm amber key light and orange rim light against deep blue space and cool teal shadows, polished chrome and enamel-painted metal, glowing CRT screens with soft bloom, subtle film grain, rich saturated but not garish colours, no text, no lettering, no frame, no border
styles.b: 1980s retro-futurist airbrush illustration in a cyan, magenta and silver-grey palette that echoes the original CGA colours: deep space-black shadows, neon-cyan CRT glow and magenta accent lights, chrome highlights with star-burst glints, warm amber rim light on faces, faint scanline sheen on screens, film grain, no text, no lettering, no frame, no border
styles.c: 1980s 'used future' sci-fi matte painting on board: visible painterly brushwork over airbrushed gradients, warm tungsten and amber cockpit light, scuffed painted metal panels with rivets and decals without letters, chrome trim, green-and-amber CRT phosphor glow, heavy film grain and slight halation like a scanned 1984 book cover, no text, no lettering, no frame, no border

tails.place: Wide cinematic 16:9 key art, no readable text, no lettering, no logo. Keep the upper third calmer so a title logo can be placed over it.
tails.portrait: Bust portrait, facing the viewer, centred, head and shoulders filling most of the square frame, at his bridge station: softly out-of-focus console with glowing CRT screens behind him. Keep the character's species, face shape, hair, eyes and clothing colours from the reference image, but redraw it as a high-quality painting.
tails.ship: A single spaceship in a front three-quarter view, centred, whole ship visible with generous margin, on a plain pure black background with no stars and no planet, so it can be cut out. Keep the silhouette and colour layout of the tiny pixel sprite in the reference image.
